2. The petitioner being the pre-emptor instituted Miscellaneous Case No.11 of 1994 in the court of the Senior Assistant Judge, 5th Court, Naogaon against the opposite parties for pre-emption of the case land under section 96 of State Acquisition 7 and Tenancy Act alleging inter alia, that the pre-emptor is a co-sharer in the case holding \ by purchase by a registered kabala dated 4.2.91 and that the opposite party No.2 transferred the case land to opposite party i.No.1 by a registered kabala dated 10.2.1992 without serving any notice on the pre-emptor under section 89 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The pre-emptee is a, stranger purchaser. The pre-emptor learnt about the transfer in question when the surveyor was surveying the case land on 6.4.94 and then obtained the Certified copy of the kabala and learnt definitely about the sale on 13.4.94. 

 6. Being aggrieved the pre-emptor being the petitioner moved this court and obtained the present rule. 7. Mr. S. N. Goswami, the learned Advocate for the petitioner does not appear to support the rule. Mr. Md. Asad Hossain Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appears on behalf of the opposite party No. l. I have perused the impugned judgment of both the courts below. It appears that the only dispute is with regard to the co-sharer ship of the pre-emptor in the case holding. The trial court has found that the pre-emptor is a co-sharer is the case holding by purchase while the lower appellate court has found that the pre-emptor is not a co-sharer in the case holding by purchase. The lower court records had not been called for at the time of issuance of the rule. The trial court has noticed that the pre-emptors case that he is a co-sharer in the case holding is not denied or challenged by the pre-emptee. The lower appellate court, on the other hand, noticed that in the application for pre-emption case land has been described with reference to, former C.S. Khatian No.82, former plot' No.331, R.S. Khatian No.150, R.S. Dag No.187. In the kabala dated 4.2.99 S.A. Khatian has been mentioned as Khatian No.88 and R.S. 663. The lower appellate court thereafter held the pre-emptor is not a co-sharer in the case holding on the basis of his purchase by the kabala dated 4.2.1991. In the application filed under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, it has been stated in paragraph No.4 that "It is submitted that the learned Appellate court below was fairly correct in holding in the tone of the learned Assistant Judge that the case was not bad for defect of party and the case was not barred by limitation and that the opposite party No. 1 was a stranger purchaser and that no sale notice was served upon the co-sharer in the case jute; but the learned Appellate court below was not correct in holding that the petitioner was not entitled to have the land preempted in as much as he was not a co-sharer tenant in the joie as no Khatian number or plot number was incorporated in his basic title deed dated 4.2.91 although factually C.S. Khatian No.82 and plot numbers had been very quoted in the petitioners sale deed dated 4.9.91." This clear statement has not been controverted by the opposite party No. l. It thus appears that the learned Appellate court misconstrued the schedule of the property as described in the kabala dated 4.2.91 in as much as in the said kabala dated 4.2.91 C. S. Khatian No.82 along with plot Nos. has been mentioned, C.S. Khatian No.82 in the kabala dated 4.2.91 and C.S. Khatian 82 in the schedule of the case land being the same, it can be concluded that the pre-emptor is a co-sharer by purchase in the case holding. The trial court has noticed that the pre-emptee did not challenge that the pre-emptor is not a co-sharer in the case holding by purchase. It thus appears that the learned Subordinate Judge has committed an error of law in reversing the decision of the trial court on the finding that the pre-emptor is not a co-sharer by purchase in the case holding which has resulted in an error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice and calls for interference by this court.
